# Repair a scientifically inconsistent HMMRATAC workflow

The supplied directory contains a pinned snapshot of MACS3, including the real
HMMRATAC implementation used to infer accessible chromatin from ATAC-seq
fragments. The offline reproduction exposes an unexpected behavior: adding a
genomic exclusion mask can change model-input statistics and derived behavior on
chromosomes that are not covered by the mask.

Inspect the HMMRATAC documentation in `source/` and the complete
fragment-to-model call graph, and repair the implementation so the exclusion mask
has the intended scientific meaning throughout the workflow. The repair must work
for ordinary paired-end fragment data and count-bearing single-cell fragment data,
preserve half-open interval semantics, and keep count and barcode bookkeeping
consistent for count-bearing fragment data.

Duplicate retention and duplicate-related CLI naming are intentionally outside
the scope of this task. Preserve the existing duplicate policy and do not add,
remove, rename, or reinterpret duplicate flags. Repeated coordinates in the
fixtures are there to verify that blacklist filtering preserves the existing
record multiplicity and count/barcode a

ATAC-seq where the DNA fragments in the sequencing library are
enriched in certain genomics regions with potential allele biases; the
second type, called `CTRL` for control, is from genomic assay in which
the DNA enrichment is less biased in multiploid chromosomes and more
uniform across the whole genome (the later one is optional). In order
to run `callvar`, please sort (by coordinates) and index the BAM
files. Example:

1. Sort the BAM file:
    $ samtools sort TREAT.bam -o TREAT_sorted.bam
    $ samtools sort CTRL.bam -o CTRL_sorted.bam
2. Index the BAM file:
    $ samtools index TREAT_sorted.bam
    $ samtools index CTRL_sorted.bam
3. Make sure .bai files are available:
    $ ls TREAT_sorted.bam.bai
    $ ls CTRL_sorted.bam.bai

To call variants:
    $ macs3 callvar -b peaks.bed -t TREAT_sorted.bam -c CTRL_sorted.bam -o peaks.vcf

events.text:
Implemented the HMMRATAC exclusion-mask repair.

The blacklist is now applied to fragment observations before EM fitting, fragment-length statistics, signal-track generation, pileup normalization, HMM training, and decoding. This prevents masked fragments from changing learned behavior on unrelated chromosomes.

Key changes:

- Updated the workflow in [hmmratac_cmd.py](/workspace/task/source/MACS3/Commands/hmmratac_cmd.py:125) to filter the finalized fragment track before model processing.
- Added in-place half-open interval filtering for ordinary paired-end fragments in [PairedEndTrack.py](/workspace/task/source/MACS3/Signal/PairedEndTrack.py:343).
- Added count-aware filtering for single-cell FRAG records in [PairedEndTrack.py](/workspace/task/source/MACS3/Signal/PairedEndTrack.py:1020), applying the same selection to coordinates and barcode arrays.
- Recomputed totals, count-weighted lengths, average template length, chromosome membership, and barcode bookkeeping after filtering.
- Preserved endpoint semantics: `[fragment_start, fragment_end)` only overlaps `[mask_start, mask_end)` when `fragment_start < mask_end` and `fragment_end > mask_start`.
- Preserved repeated-record multiplicity and surviving count/barcode associations.
- Left duplicate policy and all duplicate-related CLI behavior unchanged.

Validation passed:

- `python reproduce.py` exits successfully with both PE and FRAG cases reported as `consistent`.
- Tested exact boundary contact, overlapping and unsorted masks, chromosomes absent from the mask, whole-chromosome removal, empty masks, repeated coordinates, and 30 randomized PE/FRAG cases.
- Rebuilt the Cython extensions and passed `git diff --check`.

The public result is available at [public_reproduction_report.json](/workspace/task/outputs/public_reproduction_report.json). Additional focused verification reports remain under `outputs/`.
